Now I'll view one reference from 8 different classes.

This is an almost identical match. The reference Bugwood_23 (image #1572826) shows green tomato stems on brown paper with extensive white cottony Sclerotinia mycelium — exactly like the test image (#1572831, sequential Bugwood number from the same series). Let me use my last view on a different class.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: A green tomato stem piece laid on brown paper, with dense white fluffy/cottony mycelium spreading from the tissue. Classic Sclerotinia presentation.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot Bugwood_23** (image #1572826): Nearly identical — green stem pieces on brown paper inside a clear tray, covered in white cottony Sclerotinia mycelium. The test image is #1572831, a sequential Bugwood image from the same shoot.
- **Other candidates ruled out**: Gray_Mold shows gray-brown mold on fruit; Rhizopus shows dark sporangia (microscopic); Southern_Blight shows white mycelium at soil line but on an intact root system; Alternaria shows dark stem cankers.
